relations.evidence: ANSI joins support three types of join: inner joins, left outer joins, and right outer joins.

relations.subject: n1ql:join
relations.evidence: For more information and examples, see [ANSI JOIN Clause](../n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/join.md#section%5Fek1%5Fjnx%5F1db).

relations.subject: n1ql:join
relations.evidence: To chain joins, nests, and unnests, use the right-hand side of one JOIN, NEST, or UNNEST clause as the left-hand side of the next.

relations.subject: n1ql:join
relations.evidence: If there is no corresponding data object on the right-hand side of the join, fields from the right-hand side are missing or null.

notable_absence.finding: No privilege table is restated here, unlike the n1ql/ reference page for JOIN (which names Basic->Read / Advanced->Query Read). Consistent with the batch-wide pattern of guides omitting access-control tables that their corresponding statement-reference pages carry.

cross_component_finding: This guide's join-type walkthrough (inner/left outer/right outer, each with its own figure, worked example, and NULL-handling callout) is presented with more procedural depth than the n1ql/ reference page, which names the same three types only in passing while documenting the ANSI JOIN grammar as a whole. This is this batch's second-clearest case (after index-advisor.md's session object) of a guide surfacing enumerable structure that the reference page left implicit rather than modeled explicitly.
